utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to all of you, to the Prosecution, to the Defence counsel, to the accused, and to all the people working in this courtroom. First of all, I have to issue an oral decision in open session. Thereafter, I shall ask to move for a few minutes to private session. First decision. The Trial Chamber is issuing a decision on the admission of evidence through Witness DH who testified on the 21st of March, 2007. The Trial Chamber decided to admit the Prosecution evidence through list IC 00505 on the ground that they do present some probative value and are relevant. The Trial Chamber specifies that Exhibits P 09913 and P 09914 are admitted under seal. Mr. Registrar, you have the floor because you, too, have an IC number I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. The OTP response to the list of documents tendered by 3D through Witness van der Weijden shall be given Exhibit number IC 513. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Let's move into private session for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In open session, the cross-examination is going to proceed with Mr. Praljak. I believe he has still a few questions; then Ms. Alaburic will have one hour for her cross-examination, and we shall finish the day by giving the floor to the accused as scheduled since last week. Mr. Usher, please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir. Please sit down. Mr. Praljak, you have the floor. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Cross-examination by the Accused Praljak:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Draper. As we did not finish reviewing the video material yesterday, I would like the AV booth to prepare the video footage while I ask some questions. You learnt, sir, that approximately 36 members of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina defended the village of Stupni Do. Did you ask for and obtain the names of the members of BH army in that village? I'm asking you this because maybe we could later by comparison establish which of the victims were civilians and which were members of the BH army. So did you find out the names of the BH army members in the village?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only through witness interviews, and I wouldn't have -- I don't think I got the names of everyone. As the witnesses were interviewed, they were asked if they were a member of the defender force. So name -- we got names, though I don't think we got them an all. We didn't have -- we weren't able to interview all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how many names you were given?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you find out from talking to the witnesses that members of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Stupni Do were dressed some in uniform, some in civilian clothes? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that a lot of them were -- lived in the village, so they would dress in their normal clothes. If they had regular uniforms of the BHI -- BiH, I'm not too sure on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 27th of October, you noted -- in fact, you and your team found 16 victims. When in March, 1994, you concluded your investigation saying there were 37 victims in Stupni Do, can you tell me how the number of victims increased progressively over the months? If there were 16 in October, how many more were there in November, December, January, and February? Can you give me an idea of the timetable of increase of victims in Stupni Do until the end of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. At the beginning of the end of the investigation, we had 16 bodies from the initial investigation, and then we obtained the list of people that were still living and people that were deceased or not accounted for. These people that were deceased or not accounted for were that list of 38 I think you're referring to. As time progressed and we did interviews, witnesses would come forward and say they -- for example, one was missing seven members of his family and couldn't account for them; then as time progressed and they returned to the village and rummaged or went through the wreckage of their houses, they located the rest of their family members. And as this progressed through November, they were eventually able to account for the rest of the remaining family members and bodies that are on that list of 38 that's included in my report. Some of the bodies were recovered and, I believe, brought to the mortuary later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Perhaps the usher could assist the witness with his headset; otherwise, he's going to be in for a long one hour. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Draper, please don't give me explanations I did not ask for. My question is precise and clear. Can you give an answer to this Trial Chamber as to how the number of victims increased progressively over the months in the course of your investigation? How many victims did you have on the 27th? How many there were on record in November, in December, January, and February? How did the number of victims increase over the months? If you can't do that, tell me so.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The original number of victims were pretty well from the outset that list of 38. Confirmation of them didn't come until witnesses were interviewed and confirmed that they had recovered the bodies or portions of the bodies or what was left of the bodies. That's the best answer I can give you, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm not getting anywhere much. The original number was 16, but can you answer this: If all the remaining villagers had withdrawn to the free territory of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and all of them knew one another, most of them had the same surname, how was it possible for people not to know where their five or six family members were, and how was it possible for them to only find out several months later? Didn't you ever have suspicions about the fact that the population of one rather small village finds out that they were missing a dozen members, a dozen men, a couple of months later and they were all located within a relatively small area? Did you have any suspicions then?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I probably didn't explain myself. All the bodies were pretty well recovered in November as soon as the villagers got home. I didn't confirm it until I was able to interview these individuals, and being able to track them down and interview them took me up to March 1990. The bodies themselves were recovered fairly quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who recovered those bodies? Your team found them, or did people tell you they recovered them?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: People told me that they recovered them, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. According to witness statements and to what you concluded with -- after witness interviews, they said that there were approximately 150 people in the village in two or three houses, and they managed to fend off the attack with hand grenades. So 150 people using hand grenades. In that village, from what we heard, there were death squadrons of -- from Apostoli and Maturice armed with RPGs and other heavier weapons, and all of them managed to pull out, reach the HVO check-point, and retreat towards Breza. Never mind where. Please tell me, how was it possible, and how do you explain that 150 people did not surrender, wielded hand grenades? They were surrounded by HVO units with rocket launchers, RPGs, hand-held rocket launchers, and that group was not captured, was not killed, a group of 150 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: With respect, Your Honour, I don't think it's fair to ask the witness to answer that question. It calls for too much speculation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow me, I'd like to say why the question of General Praljak is appropriate. In the documentation the Prosecution provided with this witness, we have a witness statement from Halid Likic who was a member of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and he was a radio operator in Stupni Do. He said that he was based in a schoolhouse, and he tried to contact the command of the BH army in Boduzelj to get assistance and protection from the UNPROFOR. The command of the BH army did promise him that assistance, and that's probably the reason why BH army members decided to stay in the village and try to defend it. In that sense, I believe this question is absolutely legitimate and justified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have heard the question, the objection as well. General Praljak put a purely military question to you. He's asking for a military explanation. In military terms, are you able to answer or not? If you're not, just say so and then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the question should be somewhat amended as put by Mr. Praljak. Here mention is made of 150 individuals; and in General Praljak's question, these people suddenly become 150 men. So I don't know how suddenly all these individuals are being identified as being males. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Trechsel, I don't know if I said that. One hundred fifty people, I said, not men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It says "men."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed on line 23, "there was a group of 150 people." You probably said in your language men or so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's mistake. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's corrected now, so let's move on. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said precisely 150 people, some of which were members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; and according to witness testimony we heard here, they were defending themselves with a couple of hand grenades. Opposed to them is what I'm talking about and what we read in the report notorious Maturice units wielding RPGs, hand-held Zolja rocket launchers who blew off roofs, et cetera. That's what I'm asking the witness. If a massacre was attempted against a village and people were defending themselves with only hand grenades, how come there was no capture of those people? They were not massacred, instead they managed to retreat towards the woods. If you don't know the answer to this question, it's fine. It's a military question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Without going into speculations, do you have an answer to this question or do you not have an answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the interviews I did, it appeared that the BiH defenders, once their trench areas were overrun, they returned to the shelter areas and then one shelter told the people to run their shelter -- their lines had been overrun so run for the woods. And some did; some didn't. And the remaining BiH defenders that stayed in the village stayed around the shelter areas. I had assumed just to protect their families. As for a military point of view, I can't give any -- any insight there because I was -- all my career I've been a military policeman, not so much a soldier on that aspect. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All that is true. But in the concluding remarks of the report that you wrote and that was submitted to the United Nations, there was clearly indicated what the intent of the HVO was. It's inconceivable how somebody managed to capture all the trenches and then let through all those defenders if their intention was to capture or massacre the population. Now, you were working step-by-step, and at that time I was commander of the Main Staff of the HVO. And I want to ask you: Did you feel the need, you or your superiors, to share the results of your investigation with my Main Staff or any other judicial or political authority of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That kind of information would have been looked after by BH command legal, not myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you suggest that it would be a good idea to submit that to the Main Staff so that the Main Staff can assist you in your investigation? Did you make that suggestion? I don't know whose decision it was, but did you suggest that it would be a good idea to involve the Main Staff of the HVO in your investigation?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only information I can give you there is I did submit a memorandum to BH command legal, requesting that they get ahold of HVO because I wanted to interview anyone involved in the attack on -- on Stupni Do. And a copy of that, I believe, is in my report, and results of that, I think there was two memorandums that came back that I think are also in the report from Koak [phoen], where he talked with, I think, Mr. Banic and an HVO liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After learning what you learned in Stupni Do on the 27th, Vares had not fallen yet at that time, did you attempt to go to Vares and talk to the civilian police or somebody else? Of the HVO, I mean.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I believe that we were working out of Kiseljak, and we tried to get some witness interviews first to see what had happened, and then we were restricted from doing any kind of movement --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Draper.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- because we weren't allowed to -- we weren't allowed to go back to Vares for a while because the BiH were moving in. So for our safety, the BH command wouldn't let us leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now play again the video clip? I have some more questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Stop here, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here, next to this white little bag or sack, we see something that looks a lot like -- and I'm not sure about this. That's why I wanted to ask you. It looks a lot like a casing from an artillery barrel, and could this thing next to the bag be an artillery shell or a grenade -- a mortar grenade? Did you try to explain in your investigation what the object on the left and the object on the right are?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not go on to check whether there was a mortar shell, a piece of a mortar, or something else?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know if the BH army in Stupni Do had a mortar or any other artillery piece? Did you come by any such information?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't need the video footage any more. Could we please retrieve the -- the stills from the footage from the autopsies we saw. I will not be going into this because Judge Antonetti already asked you about the discrepancy between the charred bodies and the surroundings where the bodies were seen, which did not seem to fit into the whole picture. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] The autopsy report is which number? Can the Prosecution help me, please? I didn't write down the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: 06314 are the autopsy reports, Your Honour. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] The photographs. The Prosecutor showed them for just a second. Not the photographs, the footage that we saw for a very brief time.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I understand. These were extracts from 06318.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Prosecutor. I'm interested in the third or fourth photograph. Let's move on to the next. There's no need for ... The next one, please. Just a moment. The next one. The next one. No, not this one. Stop. Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at this photograph. I'm -- I find it actually hard to even put questions about this, but look at this area on the right-hand side, which looks like the head of an animal. Could we please play this particular sequence from the start.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Stop. Could you play it back again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this burned body? Replay it once more, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this burned body? Did you satisfy yourself to the full -- stop. The doctors who were part of your team, did they take a look at this, and did they identify this as the charred part of human body or ...

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one -- one body that the medical officers wasn't too sure if it was a human or an animal; whereas, the -- some of the medical persons thought it might be a body so we treated it as same. That was on one body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. That was all. Tell me the following: When conducting this investigation, were you guided by the fact that even a crime should be investigated within certain standards, and that one needs to be guided by the factual findings as they will, in fact, lead to the truth and only such an investigation based on such principles can provide adequate vindication to the victims? Were you guided by such principles in your investigation?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the standards of investigations I -- I tried to abide by to get to the truth of the matter whatever that would be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, my learned friends, good morning to you all. I would like the let the Chamber know that I will be requiring a bit more time than was set aside for me, and I would kindly ask of you to grant me leave to put questions, if they are deemed relevant for you. Mr. Witness, let us first off try and thoroughly analyse the evidence shown to you by the Prosecution yesterday and discussed with you with Mr. Praljak. First, let's clear up some facts. The NordBat is the first of the UNPROFOR forces to have entered Stupni Do on the 26th of October, 1993. According to their information, this took place at 1450. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What day you say? 25th?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The 26th. The 26th. You can have a look at the transcript in front of you. It will make it easier for you. Therefore, I said -- I mentioned the 26th of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If you do not know that, let's move on. Tell us -- if you don't know, tell us that you do not know because I -- every minute is precious for me. Very well --

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were the first members in there -- 25th -- I'd have to just check the report there. It's in the report, and that would be the date if that's where you got it from.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. You got in on the 27th of October; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You gave a statement to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal on the 20th, 21st, 22nd, and the 23rd of August, 1995. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: On the 22nd of March, 1994, in Zagreb, you made the footage of the scene of the crime, autopsies, and everything else that we've seen today; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zagreb, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You were on annual leave as of the 12th of December up until the 11th of January, 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 1994. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1994, in January, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Throughout the time, you predominantly dealt with the investigation into the attack on Stupni Do; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As well as my other duties, yes. Like I was the main investigator throughout my tour there for this investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. In your statement on page 3 of the B/C/S version and on page 3 of the English version, you said that when you entered the village with Major Hunter, you identified the sites where the bodies were located and you identified that there were 11 bodies there. Do you recall this statement of yours?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it's 16 bodies on the report that I gave the Tribunal investigators. I came over to Toronto, Canada when they -- when they interviewed me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Draper, let's look at your statement. I read it very carefully. I also checked the B/C/S text against the English, and the sentence literally reads: "We initially viewed a total of 11 bodies." If you wish, we may show you this part of your statement. I'm merely trying to get a confirmation from you as to whether this information contained in your statement is accurate or not.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information in the statement, if it's the one I'm thinking, is -- was taken outs of my notebook where my one -- or where my six looks like a one. So when it went into the statement, it was 11. In my notebook my 16 looks like a 1. So when we were reading my notebook, it was transcribed as 11; whereas, in actuality all the information in the reports and from witnesses it's 16.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Draper, can we therefore conclude that the information contained in your statement is inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: No, it is -- it is indeed inaccurate, or no, I disagree with you?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I disagree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You want to say that the piece of information relating to 11 bodies found there is accurate?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: With respect, I think he's already explained that there was a discrepancy in the number 11, and he explained that it should have been 16 on the basis of his notes, and I don't think there's much point in pursuing this much further. It's quite obvious that this part was inaccurate, but it's incorrect to make a sweeping statement that the statement and the information in the statement was inaccurate. Certainly the number was inaccurate at the time and he has corrected that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank my learned friend Flynn for testifying instead of Witness Draper. For this reason, I will ask Mr. Draper again, because I find his testimony relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Therefore, do you agree with the Prosecutor that the piece of information referring to 11 victims in your statement is inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 11 victims -- 11 bodies it should be, would be more accurate, and 11 bodies is -- is in the statement that was taken by the two investigators that came over to Toronto. That portion right there would be inaccurate, because it was read off my notes improperly where the 6 looks like a 1. So when we read my notes, it was 11 instead of the 16. The little loop at the end wasn't completed on the 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Draper, was this statement made in such a way that you made some written notes and then the ICTY investigators prepared or made the statement themselves, or was this statement drafted on the basis of a conversation with you which lasted over four days?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was made on the basis of their interviews of me with my notebooks in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that you misread this figure from your own notebook?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If you still have the Prosecutor's set of documents from yesterday in front of you, or else you can trust me, P 07038 -- no, P 07838, which is the letter by the United Nations Secretary-General. In item 8, it says that 14 bodies were recovered. That's on page 2, item 8, halfway through that paragraph. If we get it on e-court, you can also have a look there. Fourteen bodies were recovered in Stupni Do. This is what it says. Can you tell us where does this number of 14 recovered bodies come from?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know why. I wouldn't be able to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. To your knowledge, this statement by the UN Secretary-General is not correct; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: This question was answered yesterday, Ms. Alaburic. Yesterday, confronted with this report, the witness has said this report is not entirely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't think the witness was referring to this particular number of 14 recovered bodies, because number 14 was not mentioned yesterday at all. We spoke of the 16 recovered bodies. This is the first time we're referring to 14 recovered bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, to your knowledge, this number mentioned by the UN Secretary-General is not correct; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was the 16 bodies. So the 14 bodies, I don't know, you know, when they got their -- their information, what they based it on, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Draper, let us try to establish now how many charred bodies there were when you got there on the 27th of October, 1993. Your team was there; that is to say, in Stupni Do, also on the 28th of October. How many bodies were charred? How many did you mention?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five of the bodies didn't seem to be touched by fire at all. The rest were in some way charred, and a lot of them very charred. But the three in the cellar, the one on the upper portion of the -- on the road had a charred timber across him, and the one in the woods --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You don't have to refer to the bodies individually. Let us try and look at the total numbers, and then if there will be any need to analyse this I will ask you to do that. You said that there were five charred bodies; is that right? I'm sorry. Five were not charred. So there were nine charred bodies and two charred bodies which you weren't certain were actually human; is that right? To clarify what I'm putting to you.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I believe there was one that they weren't too sure whether it was an animal or body.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: To make a small digression from the charred bodies, in your report which the Prosecutor marked P 06978, in item 2, you said that 16 bodies were examined at seven locations, and this is the figure you use. In item 4(c) of your report, you say 14 bodies were recovered which could be said were human. Do you recall this part of your report, or do you need to consult it to see whether I'm accurately representing it?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I can just have a look at it to see while we're talking.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you should take the Prosecutor's bundle of documents, and it will save us a lot of time. Otherwise, we will waste a lot of time, because I will be putting at least 30 different statements from your reports. So we're talking about P 06978, item 4(c).

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tab number?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page number?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher assist the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I didn't make note of the pages because it's easier to locate the different points, the items, the bulleted items.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In item?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 4(c). "Fourteen bodies were found that appeared human." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, and the --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Page 6.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. And this information is based on the NordBat RMPs that had gone into the site. So this would have been on the 26th of October when the regiment MP went through, and this is what they noticed was the 14 bodies that appeared to be human.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Sir, I must admit that I fail to understand your statement that this information comes from NordBat. At this stage, for the time being, it's not important who the source of the information is. We're talking about the information contained in the report, and I should like to know from you whether you think this information is accurate or not. The information can be found in the report; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ms. Alaburic, if you look at number 4 in the report from the beginning, you see that it is a reference made to an interview with one Mr. Gustafsson, and the witness reports that Mr. Gustafsson said the following things. And if Mr. Gustafsson said that there were 14 bodies that looked human and that were found, that's it. How can the witness say something else and report something different from what someone has told him? I do not understand your question, I must say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Trechsel, if you permit me. We have the statement from this witness that 16 bodies were recovered. We have a different statement that 16 bodies were recovered but that one could say with certainty that 14 of them were human. The figure mentioning 14 persons is also referred to by the UN Secretary-General. I myself am loath to speak of victims in terms of numbers. However, since we are involved in criminal proceedings, I believe I have to go into this. At this point, we find it exceptionally important to establish whether the accurate figure is that of 14 or 16 bodies recovered at the time when they got into Stupni Do. My contention is by confronting the witness with these numbers is to establish the relevance and reliability of some of the figures contained in the documentation provided us to by the Prosecution, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, and perhaps this may help to explain it for you. I can understand Ms. Alaburic's confusion because of the number 11 put into the ICTY statement, but the witness gave evidence yesterday by referring to his report of the 15th of November, which is Exhibit 6978. And you may remember that he was guided in his evidence by the information contained at paragraphs 2 to 4 where he went through each of the crime scenes with you, and he told you what was found in the crime scenes. Now, if you examine that, you will see clearly that between scene 1 and scene 7 there were 16 bodies found. So this, in my humble submission, corroborates the fact that this man found 16 bodies with his team, and he reported that to his superiors, who reported that -- who presumably reported it on to their superiors, and eventually it should have found its way to the UN bodies in New York. And he's not in a position to explain where they came up with the 14 bodies. He reported 16 bodies, and that's clearly stated in his report of the 15th of November, 1993. There is the mention of the 14 bodies, which Ms. Alaburic has pointed out in the same report, but as Judge Trechsel has pointed out, this was quoted from the Norwegian soldiers. This is not his evidence. This was the information he received from the Norwegian soldiers, but his findings were that there were 16 bodies on site.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank my learned friend, Mr. Flynn, again for testifying. I am not confused, I must say, by the numbers, but they are confusing to anyone who to tries to really understand them. The example is this number of 16. The witness himself told us that this number of 16 may include one non-human body. Furthermore, I'm not asking this witness at all about the source of information on those 14 human bodies. I'm just asking him whether the number contained in his report is accurate. The witness can answer it is accurate, it is not accurate, or I don't know. Let us continue with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ms. Alaburic, we must be precise, and as professionals one must expect us to be precise. On page 20, line 2, you say, "In item 4(c) of your report, you say that 14 bodies were recovered." So you try to create the impression that there is a contradiction between what the witness put in his report and what he's saying now. But if you had looked carefully at this report, you would have seen that is it not the -- the witness speaking but the witness reporting what someone else told him, and I think this is muddling up things a little. I'm sorry. I do not think this is quite correct, and I think we should perhaps abandon this now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did intend to conclude with this, but let me clarify. It was not my intention to deceive anyone. I just invoked a document in a very brief passage that anyone is able to look and see the context in full. What is important is that this deals with a report of this witness and the fact that he did not question any figures. In fact, I believe that between this number and the number that the witness used, with the reservation that some bodies are not human, there is no real discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But let me proceed with another issue that I wanted to clear up with you. Let us go back to the charred bodies. Give me the exact number. How many charred bodies were found by you when you entered Stupni Do on the 26th of -- 27th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be around 11, I think. There is the five bodies that weren't really touched by any kind of burns, so that would give you 11, one which may have been animal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Witness, in the report of the UN Secretary-General, for the record P 07838, in the same passage, which is paragraph 8, we read that out of the 14 bodies that were found there were four men and three women who were identified; whereas, other bodies were charred beyond recognition, burnt beyond recognition. So according to the UN Secretary-General's report, there were seven bodies that could not be recognised. Do you believe there is a difference between the information given in your report and that of the UN Secretary-General? Witness, I would appreciate quicker answers. Because if we have to spend that much time on noticing the difference between 7 and 11, I will not be able to finish before tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. Where it says four men, two, three -- three for sure were men, three for sure were women. There might have been another man there, but I think they found that out the next day when they turned the body over -- or the charred remains over .

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm just asking you, is there a difference between the number of charred bodies used in your report and the number used by the UN Secretary-General? Give me yes, no, or you don't see the difference.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say. Some of the charred bodies that they're talking about can -- well, I guess what -- what I'm trying to say is there is just the five bodies that were untouched by flame, and so the rest were charred. And if he says different, that's not what I found.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, sir. Let's move on. Did you observe in autopsy reports that you obtained, and the autopsy was performed on the 31st of October, 1993, that 12 bodies were described as charred? Did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite possibly. It's probably in my report the autopsy results. I'd have to check. I just can't off the top of my mind tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Just a few words about the autopsy. In your statement, on page 15 in the B/C/S version and page 9 of the English version, you said --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There we are.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So in the statement -- I see that the pages are on record. You said that you found out about the autopsy when you tried to arrange for a post-mortem to be carried out on victims from Borovica. You were told then that the victims from Stupni Do were autopsied. Do you remember that statement, and do you standby that assertion concerning the autopsies?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that day quite well because they were giving me heck for not attending and finding out about these autopsies being done on Stupni Do bodies, but I didn't know where the bodies had gone, so this was the first I learnt of it. So once I had learnt about that I asked if I could get copies of the autopsy report, and found out that they had a video taken, too, so I asked for that too. I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you know at all that there was an intention to carry out these autopsies?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, was the video recording of the autopsies made by the team that performed the autopsies, the team made up of local Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you, but it was none of my people.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But you used that video in editing the footage in March 1994 in Zagreb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I attached the -- when the -- yeah, that video that I got from the Visoko mortuary about the autopsies was attached to that briefing that I did in Zagreb. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: At least according to the evidence presented by the Prosecutor in this case, the autopsies were performed on 20 bodies. Can you tell us who recovered and included in Stupni Do victims those bodies that were not covered by your investigation on the 27th and 28th of October?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just through interviews I had learnt that the people from the mortuary, once Stupni Do was in BiH hands again, the mortuary workers went there and recovered the bodies of three people up in the trench.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Sir. Sir. Left us separate these things. On the 31st of October autopsies were performed. Vares fell on the 3rd of October, and that's -- sorry, 3rd of November, and that's when the BH army had complete control over that area, and what you just said cannot apply to the 31st of October, 1993. Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Thanks for pointing that out. I just have to go the report where these autopsies are taking place. What tab is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the autopsies were performed on the 31st of October, 1993? Autopsy reports are under P 06314. But if you are going to review them now, you will need at least a half hour to take in the -- the summary of those reports. In that case, if you can't answer, I will move on to another question. Can you answer who it was within those two or three days -- just tell us you don't know. We will get to a real answer. At this moment you don't know who added --

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. When you were speaking about autopsies of Borovica victims that you wanted performed, can you explain to us what victims were those?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the -- it was from another investigation I assigned one of my members to carry out, and they -- NordBat had recovered the bodies, and we -- no one wanted to accept them, and we eventually got them dropped off at the Visoko mortuary. I can't remember if there was two or three. I'm not too sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us were those bodies of Croats?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they were, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Right. Can we now look at how this list of victims was made? Every time I mention the term "victims list" I will invoke P 09121, an exhibit of three pages, and I will give the page numbers. R0048864 through 66. Mr. Draper, when you were asked by General Praljak, you said that you added to that list the names of persons you were told by witnesses had been killed or had disappeared, gone missing. Witness, please don't look at that list now. I just mentioned the number for the record. Could you please focus on the question now. A while ago you answered General Praljak by saying that you, too, added to the list of victims in Stupni Do based on witness interviews.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I added to the list of living. I don't think I added to the list of -- of deceased.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll look in a moment at your statement. In your statement to the OTP, pages 17 of the B/C/S and page 10 of the English version, you said, I quote: "We did not really have a body or remains in each case --" or, rather, "We did not necessarily have a body or remains in every case. If someone was missing and another witness had seen them killed or seen them dead, I added them to the list. If we had a body I would include it, if someone was missing, but I had no indication that someone had seen him being killed or dying, then I did not put them on the list of deceased." Do you remember this statement you made, Witness, and would you make the same statement today?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's referring to my own list where I corroborate the death list or the missing list. It's not the original list. This is a list where, as I go down to each person and I corroborate their death, then I would mark it on the list, and that's the list that you're talking about R00848864.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes. So in that way you came up with a list of 38 victims.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now look at those victims. I'll focus on the most important. One of your interviewees, Ejub Likic, told you that Muamer and Sevko had been killed while in a trench. They were members of the BH army, and their bodies were detected in November 1993. That statement is recorded in document P 08121, point 27(j). These two persons -- or, rather, the three persons that I mentioned, members of the BH army, are on the list of persons killed under numbers 15 and 30. Can you agree, Witness, that on the list of victims from Stupni Do the two members of the BH army I mentioned a moment ago are also included, two persons who were killed in combat?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Those two are on these list of deceased of Stupni Do, the ones that were in the trenches up there. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The same interviewee told you the following: "Samir Rahic was running from a Serb house at the outside of the village that held nine members of the BH army towards the centre of the village where they were moving, as the attack advanced when he was hit by a sniper." That statement is mentioned in the same exhibit, paragraph 27(a) and (f). Samir Rahic is on the list of persons killed, under number 37. Can you confirm that, Witness, number 37?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The same interviewee told you that Salih Nikic was killed -- sorry, Salih Likic was killed in the vicinity of a shelter in the centre of the village that was defended by around 14 BH army members. It's recorded in the same exhibit, paragraph 27(ai). Salih Likic is also on the list of 38 persons killed, under number 27.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Another interviewee, Serifa Likic, said that while they were in hiding, an elderly woman died, later identified as Rasida Likic, and the probable cause of death was exhaustion or heart attack. The statement was recorded in Exhibit P 06978, paragraph 19 F. Rasida Likic is on the list of 38 Stupni Do victims under number 22. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we now agree, after all of this, that the list of victims also includes names of BH army members who were killed in combat?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's contained on that list of 38 list of deceased at Stupni Do. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this list also contained the name of at least one person who is known not to have been killed in Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who would that be?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Rasida Likic, who died in the woods due to exhaustion or as a result of a heart attack, as witnessed by Serifa Likic. She's number 22 on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, Ms. Alaburic. I'm a little bit confuse. When we're talking about the list, are we talking about the list of deceased Annex A?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Flynn, at the beginning of this passage, I said clearly that I will be referring to the list of 38 persons killed, which is part of Exhibit P 09121, and I quoted the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: 8121. And the page number again is -- because the reason I'm asking is that I'm looking at the list, and I'm looking at the number that you're giving for the deceased person and it doesn't correspond with what's on my list.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. I have been giving you the wrong number all this time. It's in fact 08121. It's simply wrongly recorded in my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: It's not so much that but it's the individual deceased. For example, Rasida Likic is on Annex A as listed as number 13, but you have given her as number 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Yes. I wouldn't like to stop you, Madam Alaburic, and I fully respect the rights of the Defence to go on. But, first of all, I believe that probably your time is already off, and the greffier may give us an indication what is the time that is allotted to us about that issue. But, as number two, I would also like to say that with all due respect to everything you and Mr. Praljak have asked today and yesterday, I really would like to draw your attention to the fact that -- that the issues connected to Stupni Do, they are adjudicated facts, and we had -- I mean, this Tribunal had a judgement on -- about Ivica Rajic. And that is why I really feel that many of the questions which you raised somehow, at least to me, do not seem to be in a way those which might help the Defence to establish the facts. Therefore, I have to say that you have to ask questions which are -- which are about the rights of your -- of your accused and those issues which would help you to establish the facts, and not about speaking about autopsies and if one person was a human being or an animal, et cetera. Really, I do not feel that it contributes to what you would like to establish. It is my advice, and again I would say that I am not at all trying to -- to prevent the Defence to do its work, but simply I would like to refer to the facts which have already been established and determined by this Tribunal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Judge Prandler, I wish to tell you the following: With connection -- in connection with Stupni Do, there are no adjudicated facts. The events and the attack on Stupni Do on the 23rd of October, 1993, have not been discussed in this case. What does exist is a plea agreement that Mr. Rajic made with the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal and the decision of the Tribunal on sentencing that was based on that plea agreement. What Ivica Rajic confirmed in his plea agreement or contested is of no relevance to us. We believe that our clients must be presumed innocent in full until their responsibility for the events in Stupni Do of that day is proven. As for events in Stupni Do, like in any criminal proceedings, it is important to establish the facts that are alleged by the Prosecution that on a certain day a certain unit attacked a certain village causing a certain number of victims. The indictment refers to 38 victims, and it is of crucial importance for us to establish whether it is indeed the correct number of victims, how the lists were compiled that were later used by the Prosecution to bring this indictment. At the beginning of my examination, I said that I was extremely embarrassed to speak of people and, moreover, victims in terms of numbers. But if the Prosecution alleges that there were 38 victims of the HVO attack on Stupni Do, then it is not only my right but also my obligation to explore whether it is justified to claim the existence of even one victim. I do not want to short sell a single victim of any attack whatsoever, but it is our duty to determine all the relevant facts. And it would be contrary to the elementary rules of my profession to just skip over or gloss over the allegations in the indictment just because we are embarrassed to discuss the victims. In fact, you raised a very interesting topic, and maybe my colleagues wish to make a contribution as well. Honourable Judge Prandler, I have a feeling that in the Vares case a military verdict has already been made, but maybe I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Alaburic, for your explanation, clarification, and I am grateful to you for this. I would like to say that when I mentioned adjudicated facts, I mentioned it not in the sense of a legal term but in a way that what happened in Stupni Do had also been investigated by various organs before, including of course those who had been in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Your papers which you submitted to us in this -- in this bundle, there are many documents which deal with the investigations which -- which HVO actually initiated and which led to the establishment of certain facts. It is what I wanted to say, that those facts had been established, although they have not been included as "adjudicated" facts. It was what I was saying, that to find the true it is not related to autopsies and one or two victims or 13 or 14, but what you would need indeed to show that how your accused are not -- are not involved in those which happened in Stupni Do. And it is from this intention -- my intention was really to help you and not to in a way taking those very technical questions which the witness was not aware of, et cetera, but to -- to speak about those issues which would really help you to establish the facts as far as Stupni Do is concerned. So it is my intention only and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just be heard on this point, because we've spent now the last two weeks listening to testimony which has really been about nothing else except the victims in Stupni Do, and I -- if Your Honour does take that view, I'm very surprised that two weeks ago Your Honour did not say to the Prosecution, "Why are we about to spend two weeks on this subject that has already been adjudicated in the Rajic case?" And for Your Honour now to say that -- that -- Your Honour, we've said before that the Judges of the Trial Chamber in the system under which we operate in do not know what the Defence case is in advance and do not know the nature of all the evidence. Your Honour, I have to say once again it's a very, very serious matter that Your Honour should take that view without allowing the Defence to complete its cross-examination and perhaps down the road other evidence to be given that will indeed reflect on the position of these accused. Your Honour, I have to put on the record my concern about that, Your Honour's intervention. I know it was well-intentioned, but it does raise the issue again of fairness between the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may be heard briefly. I'm even more concerned because here we are now months into the process, and it would appear, and I am saying this with all due respect, but it would appear that members of the Bench do not understand the process in this Tribunal. They don't understand that this is an adversarial setting. They don't understand the presumption of innocence in a sense. They don't understand that the Prosecution has the burden of proof, and now we're pre-judging the events. Last -- two weeks ago I indicated that perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I wish to be heard, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, I won't allow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I wish to be heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I won't allow you to say the Judges do not understand the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am just saying, Your Honour --.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a pure fabrication.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- if it was a pure fabrication, then perhaps we would not have this aberration of a trial compared to other trials in this Tribunal. We would not be have a Trial Bench saying you can do this in your case, recognising that the Defence may not have a case to answer, yet the burden has been shifting. We have been trying slowly, gently to educate this Trial Bench to adopt the procedure based on the rules of evidence and based on the Statute, and I'm extremely concerned. And I think again we need to have a hearing to discuss whether or not this trial can proceed or whether we should start afresh, because I'm concerned. Given those comments that we just heard, there seems to have been decisions that have already been made, without even hearing all of the evidence, without giving the Defence an opportunity to be heard. And we're well advanced into the case, and it appears, in my humble opinion, that members of the -- of the Bench, perhaps all of them, perhaps some, I don't know, fully do not understand that the Prosecution has the burden of proof throughout this trial, and this Tribunal and this Trial Bench is strictly here to determine whether the Prosecution at the conclusion of its evidence has met its burden. And that's what I want to say, and again we need to have this hearing. It has to go well beyond the one hour that we're going to have this afternoon to hear from the clients. And I apologise if I have to speak so directly and sharply, but I think it is high time that we get our house in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute, Mr. Stewart. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Your Honour Prandler, it is not up to us to show, as Ms. Alaburic said, that we had nothing to do with Stupni Do. It seemed to me so far that the Prosecution should have been asked to respond to the following: What has the commander of the Main Staff, who was 300 kilometres away, to do with someone whose facts we are determining 14 years later? We're talking about victims whose numbers have not been established, and many have been appearing in Zenica, and no criminal proceedings were brought to a close. This has not led anywhere. Another thing, Your Honour. It is extremely important as to whether the units the way they were described as hordes, in fact, attacked a village, where at least 193 persons were able to flee. And this of course has to do with the joint criminal enterprise against us. Did these units within the joint criminal enterprise and under my command, in fact enter the village and attack it to kill 120 to 150 persons? Were there among them individuals, smaller groups of people who were mad, intoxicated, drugged, or sick who committed the crimes that we heard of from this witness? We heard about a woman being killed, a man whose throat was slit, and so on and so forth. But all these facts, even if we engage all of our imagination, the Prosecution not once said what the link was between all those other structures and this group. Did Mr. Praljak in fact organise units, issue orders or spread ideas that something like that should be done? If this is not the crucial matter, if this is an adjudicated fact, then I'm going back to what I initially said. Why are we wasting our time? Left us draft the judgement. I believe that what we have to do here is to establish how the number 16 ended up as being 36. What sort of propaganda was there? Were these soldiers wearing a uniform, or were they in civilian clothes? We need to examine a crime by certain standards as the crime has a certain scale. It reaches down to some individuals but does it reach up to Mr. Praljak? If it does, then in your judgement you will render an adequate sentence. We have not, however, established this so far. The Prosecution, you should produce a single piece of evidence that would link us up with those crimes. Let me give you another example. How many generals should, in fact, be tried for what is going on in Iraq? If we look at all those victims and bodies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: We will have to have a break because of technical reasons. I understand your emotions absolutely, but I think it's not the moment to go on very long in that direction because nobody, nobody has in any way made any allusion to the responsibility of the accused. Nothing of that kind was said. It was a remark which did not, did not refer to the issue of -- of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, shall I make my intervention after the break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Let me also -- allow me to answer to those questions which are also brought up by Mr. Praljak and others. Again, I would like to say, and I would like to repeat also what Judge Trechsel underlined a few minutes ago, that nobody on the Bench are questioning and making any determination as far as the issue of Stupni Do in relation to the accused. My point was that the -- there are many other issues which could be, in my view at least, more usefully explored by the Defence. And I also refer to those documents which are submitted by Madam Alaburic, which for example contains an order from the Minister of Defence for Herceg-Bosna asking investigation of the -- of the issues which -- and the events which happened in Stupni Do. It is what I said, that these issues could be more explored and then to take into account. And it shows that your own leadership that time was very much -- very much involved in investigation and finding out what -- what was the -- what was really the truth about Stupni Do. And it was my point, and it was my intention, to ask you to speak about this issue and those which are facts. They were more important than some technical details, and that is why I again underline that nobody pre-judge the accused here. I didn't speak about the accused. I spoke about the method of the questioning. I spoke about how the Defence should concentrate on certain important points.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be allowed. I would only like to make one point in response to Judge Prandler. My cross-examination consists of two parts. In the first part, I wish to analyse the probative value of the documents produced by the Prosecution and on which the indictment rests. In the second part, I wish to show on the basis of my own documents what I believe is part of our Defence case concerning Vares. Had you allowed me to conclude my cross-examination, you would have realised what my intention was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Mindua has a question and then we'll have the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's not really a question I want to put. Unfortunately, we don't have enough time. I just wanted to make a comment to the Defence. First of all to you, Mr. Karnavas. You have always made a very useful contribution to the debates before this Chamber, but I'm quite astonished by the sharpness and the harshness of your language when you say that the Trial Chamber does not understand the Rules of Procedure that apply in this jurisdiction. I hope that Mr. Karnavas will soon change -- have a change of feelings about this. Mr. Praljak, let me tell you that the judgement has not been drafted yet, of course. Of course, Mr. Praljak is right to say that the burden of proof is for the Prosecution. The Prosecution has to establish the links between the crimes. And the accused are sitting here, so I would like to assure the accuse on that matter and remind the Prosecution of its task here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 10 to 11.00. We'll resume at 10 past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing is resume without Judge Mindua who has to sit on the other case. He told me that he would not be able to attend the rest of the hearing today. He'll come back in this case next week. Mr. Stewart, before I give you the floor, I'd like to make the following comment: With respect to the documents that were submitted to the witnesses, we've noticed significant discrepancies in terms of the persons, the individuals who were killed in that village. In the witness statement, the figure of 11 bodies is mentioned. Apparently, the witness said when he arrived in the village he found 16 bodies. That's the first discrepancy; and then we see that in the report of the Secretary-General to the Security Council there is a third figure, a figure of 14 bodies. And when you look at the indictment, you find the figure of 38 bodies. Thanks to the questions put by both parties, we come to realise that there might be a case where a body was either that of a human or of an animal. Furthermore, there is another figure that could have been mentioned by the Defence. The Defence might want to do this, but we are not aware of this. As far as I'm concern, what I did is was I counted the number of autopsy reports, and I came to a total of 20 autopsy reports. That's a new figure that comes into it. Twenty bodies were taken to the morgue, 20 bodies, so another figure appears now. And whilst we were discussing this, I had a look at these 20 reports, and it appears that three of these bodies have been identified as bodies of the members of the ABiH; not one, not two, but three. Salko Likic, Muamer Likic, and Sefkija Likic are the individuals concerned. In the autopsy reports, it is stated that these individuals were members of the ABiH. These were not charred bodies. I had the feeling, and I believe that Judge Prandler shared my view, I had the feeling that these salient points of the autopsy reports could have been taken up by the Defence during the cross-examination to be clarified with the witness, rather than going into a lengthy discussion about the figures in the report to the Security Council. Because the document we have here, which is the -- our working document, is the -- is the document where -- that refers to 20 bodies being taken to the morgue. I'm not sure Ms. Alaburic was about maybe to refer to these documents, but there are a lot of questions that could be put to the witness on the basis of the autopsy reports. These autopsy reports raise a number of issues. When my fellow Judge took the floor, he just wanted to focus the attention of the Defence on that point, and I myself was about to do the same, because we have a number of questions about this based on these autopsy reports. The witness might be in a position to clarify these points. That's why we wanted to invite the Defence to better focus on these issues that seem significant to us if we want to really find out what actually took place. Ms. Alaburic, you have the floor again for you to be able to conduct a productive cross-examination, to try and clarify a number of points.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you very much. I would wish to remind, and this is recorded on page 26, line 18 of today's transcript, my question concerning the autopsy and 20 bodies. Thereupon, I asked the witness as to how he was able to account for the discrepancy between these figures and the figures contained in the earlier document, regardless of whether the figure mentioned was 14 or 16 and the witness answered that he could not account for the discrepancy. I myself did not deal in great detail with the autopsy reports. I tried to decipher them and take them from the legal -- from the medical context into the legal context, but I did not wish to inquire the witness about the autopsy reports because the witness himself said that he did not consider himself to have the adequate expertise, and as a military policeman he could not examine with me these medical documents. Now, Your Honours, let me tell you what my intention is in my cross-examination, and I would also like the witness to know what it is that I wish to demonstrate. I wish to demonstrate that after the HVO left Stupni Do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, Ms. Alaburic. You're absolutely right. But I'd like to draw your attention to the first autopsy report that should have raised a number of questions. This is the report related to Samir Rahic. Reading this report, I see that he died apparently on the 22nd of October, whereas if you look at all the other reports they mention that the individuals concerned died on the 23rd of October. So how come we have someone who died one day before everyone else? Furthermore, if you look at the second page of the report, you find that this body was completely charred. There's a mystery here. The witness might be in a position to clarify this and tell us what happened when he conducted the investigation. Did he find out maybe that some people were killed before the 23rd? It might be a simple mistake in this document in the date. This person may have died on the 23rd, but that's something that should be clarified. I did not want to intervene at the beginning because I do not want to interfere with the conduct of the cross-examination, but that's typically one of the problems we sometimes identify during the cross-examination and where we wonder why the Defence counsel do not raise these issues, because these are significant issues, in our view.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since neither the witness nor any of his associates took part in the autopsy process, they merely received these autopsy reports, I did not deem it necessary to put any questions to the witness concerning these autopsies, but I do thank you for your comment that with regard to victim number 1, Samir Rahic. It is indeed written in the autopsy report that he died on the 22nd of October, 1993. We can therefore ask the witness whether he can tell us anything with regard to the date of death of this person who is contained in the list of victims from Stupni Do, dated the 23rd of October -- 22nd of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe you're referring to deceased number 38. Is that the one? And, if so, from witness statements and that he did die on the 23rd. A lot of the documents that I was looking over, there were mistakes here and there, maybe, you know, a date of birth or that type of thing so --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: If I may, the witness -- the deceased does appear as number 36 on the list, not number 38.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh. That would be correct. It would be the 23rd of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me remind you that precisely in connection with this person I put a question to the witness in connection with the statement by Ejub Likic who said that this person Samir Rahic on the 23rd came out of a Serb house and ran toward the centre the village when he was hit by a sniper. In my view, therefore, this is just a typographical error and he indeed was killed on the 23rd of October. If you allow me, I would like to tell you briefly what my intention is in my cross-examination. I wish to establish that Muslims were in Stupni Do in the night between the 23rd and the 24th --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the night between the 22nd and the 23rd of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and that the villages remained in the area thereafter. Therefore, when UNPROFOR entered the village, they did not come across the village in the state in which the village was when the HVO left. I would also like to say that there were local HVO units in the area, or to be precise there were two also HVO units there. Many witnesses said the same, and there are many HVO documents which -- there are many army of Bosnia-Herzegovina official documents to that effect. Furthermore, if I will have any time left, I will try to show that there were attempts on the parts of the Bosnia-Herzegovina official authorities to establish the events in Stupni Do as well as the fact there was the attempts by the government of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna to that effect, and I will also deal with the change of name on the part of Ivica Rajic and some other matters. My colleague tells me that on page 45, line 6, you will see what it is about on the basis of my questions. I will not belabour the point now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, based on your own statement, and that's page 13 in the B/C/S text and page 8 of the English version, you were in Stupni Do where you spoke with the mayor, Husnija Mahmutovic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What date was that? The 12th?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of November, according to your statement.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I remember being --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. You were there. The date isn't important. You said that the mayor told you that one place, which was marked on the map as just a pile of ash and bones, that this one thing was not there when he was in Stupni Do on the 23rd of October, 1993, in the night. Do you recall Husnija Mahtovic telling you that he was in Stupni Do in the night of the 23rd of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that a pile of ash, of ashes or bones, that you saw there in November, Mahmutovic had not seen when he was in Stupni Do on the 23rd of October, 1993, according to his statement?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't confirm. I'm just wondering if that's the one that he was -- that we maybe thought might have been an animal or a human.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you say literally, "The mayor informed us that one location which was marked on the map as a pile of ashes and bones had not been there when he was in Stupni Do in the night of the 23rd of October, 1993." Did you faithfully convey Mr. Mahmutovic's statement in this statement of yours?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That statement was put in -- in the report because that's information that he gave to me. So I put that in there because it was -- it didn't corroborate the investigation at that time or didn't flow in with everything that we knew. So I thought that significant, and that's why I put it in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Draper, do you remember that your collocutor, your interviewee, Rasim Dafo, also told you that he had returned to the village the night after? Rasim Dafo, D-A-F-O.

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were several soldiers who went around that night to look for other survivors. He may be one of them. I would have check that report to make sure that he indeed was him, but off the top of my mind I can't tell you. There were several. Can you give me a page or -- it doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I could give you more names of persons whom you interviewed and who said that they had returned to the village, but it is enough for me that you confirm several of the interviewees said so. Is it accurate that several of your interviewees said they had returned to the village on the 23rd of October after the HVO left the village?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us see what UN Secretary-General says about this in his report. It's P 07838, paragraph 6, the last sentence. I will read in B/C/S because I don't have the text in English, and I apologise for any errors in translation. "Approximately around 1630 shooting ceased. The HVO started pulling out from the village, enabling the population to return to the village and look for survivors." If we can turn to paragraph 6, the one that I quoted from, which is the next page in the report. There you see in paragraph 6, the last sentence. Mr. Draper, can you confirm that this statement in the report of the UN Secretary-General is accurate?

utterances.speaker: NELSON DRAPER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not completely accurate. The HVO enabling the population to return, they were still in the village and the people that went searching through the village had already been in there near the centre shelter area. And once the HVO pulled out, they went to the other shelter areas that they knew about looking for other survivors, and they found them and brought them all back to the main shelter, and then later on that night they -- they left the village into the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may. Sorry, Ms. Alaburic. The English version of the report of the SRSG uses the words "to go through the village looking for survivors," rather than to "return to the village," so there are two different meanings. To go through the village might imply there are still people there. To return to the village is a different connotation. The English says "to go through."

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
